theater: 河中蒲州及長春宮前線

battle.name: 河中之戰
battle.theater: 河中蒲州及長春宮前線
battle.brief: 唐德宗建中四年涇原兵變，節度使李懷光因受猜忌而反出河中。貞元元年，馬燧說降晉、隰、慈三州，陶城一戰摧其前鋒，又單騎至長春宮城下說降徐庭光，河中諸將相繼出降，李懷光自縊。卡面這柄羅馬短劍不在此役現場：它代表以刺突破盾的短兵路線，唐軍則靠環首直刃刀、槍陣與弩砲，勝負落在斷糧與攻心。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰雙方，是唐廷與河中藩鎮李懷光，並且必須放在建中四年涇原兵變的大背景裡看。朝廷一方是唐德宗李适的中央政府：涇原兵變之後德宗出奔奉天、漢中，詔令各道節度使勤王，由河東節度使馬燧以行營副元帥的名義總攝討平之師，渾瑊、駱元光、唐朝臣、李建徽各引本部兵馬與神策軍同進，河北道、隴右道以及關中行在的部隊也奉詔入援。叛方是節度使李懷光所領的河中軍：他是靺鞨人，本姓茹，父祖徙居幽州，以戰功賜姓李，先後任朔方節度使、涇原節度使，建中四年奉詔救駕有功，受封太尉、賜鐵券，隨即反出河中自保。河中藩鎮的建制與疆域在史籍中可見者，至少包括河中、絳州、晉州、隰州、慈州五州，兵源以朔方系的蕃漢混編部隊為主，糧餉則靠河東鹽池的鹽利與黃河通道。雙方指揮系統一邊是行營、節度使與宦官監軍，一邊是節度使、諸將與都虞侯，各有旗幟與符節可以調兵。第三方是朱泚的大秦政權：他以涇原節度使身份在長安稱帝，是朝廷同時必須對付的另一支力量；李懷光並未與朱泚聯合，反而退守河中，因此本役不是涇原兵變的附屬，而是一場由將領自保慾望引發的獨立叛亂。
countriesEn: This war pitted the Tang court against the Hezhong military governorship of Li Huai-guang, and it can only be read against the larger backdrop of the Jingyuan mutiny of Jianzhong 4 (783). On the court side stood the central government of Emperor Dezong of Tang, Li Shi: after the Jingyuan mutiny broke out, Dezong fled to Fengtian and then to Hanzhong, and he summoned the jiedushi of the circuits to raise troops for the emperor's relief. Ma Su, jiedushi of Hedong, was commissioned deputy commander-in-chief of the field camp, and Hun Jian, Luo Yuanguang, Tang Chaochen and Li Jianhui led their own departmental troops alongside the Divine Strategy Army, with contingents also arriving from Hebei, Longyou and the imperial travelling court. The rebel side was the Hezhong army of jiedushi Li Huai-guang: a Jiehe man born into the surname Ru, whose forebears had moved to Youzhou and who received the surname Li and the name Huai-guang for his record in battle, he had served successively as jiedushi of Shuofang and of Jingyuan, and after leading a thousand-li forced march to relieve the emperor in Jianzhong 4 he was honoured as Grand Commandant and granted an iron certificate of pardon, only to rise in revolt and retire to Hezhong to defend himself. The Hezhong command, as it appears in the historical record, covered at least the five prefectures of Hezhong, Jiangzhou, Jinzhou, Xizhou and Cizhou; its soldiers came chiefly from the mixed barbarian and Chinese troops of the Shuofang system, and its supplies rested on the salt works of the Hedong salt pans and on the Yellow River route. Command on the court side ran through the field camp, the jiedushi and eunuch supervisors; on the rebel side it ran through the jiedushi, his generals and his military commissioner. A third force must also be counted: Zhu Ci's Great Qin regime, proclaimed by the Jingyuan jiedushi at Chang'an in 783, which the court had to defeat at the same time. Li Huai-guang did not join Zhu Ci but fell back on Hezhong instead, so the present war was not a branch of the Jingyuan mutiny but an independent revolt born of a commander's instinct for self-preservation.
people: 這場戰爭裡真正決定勝負的是幾個人。李懷光是全場主角：他在奉天解圍之後自恃千里救駕卻不得見天子，屢上表揭發盧杞、趙贊、白志貞，朝廷貶三人之後又賜他太尉與鐵券，他當著使者把鐵券擲於地上說「凡人臣反，則賜鐵券，今授懷光，是使反也」，隨即舉兵，卻沒有與朱泚合流，而是退回河中自保，最後在諸將盡降、援絕糧盡之下自縊而死。馬燧是本役的實際主帥：他以河東節度使的權力與私誼，先把李懷光分守晉州、隰州、慈州的姻親要廷珍、牙將毛朝易與鄭抗一一拉過來，切斷河中的北面依托，再在陶城擊破李懷光前鋒，射殺其大將徐伯文；長春宮攻不下，他不強攻，單騎到城下直呼守將徐庭光，披襟示以無防，說出「汝曹自祿山已來，徇國立功四十餘年，何忽為滅族之計」的話，徐庭光當即率眾羅拜而降，長春宮一破，河中的門戶洞開。渾瑊、駱元光、唐朝臣三軍此前在同州、華州一線屢敗於徐庭光所率的六千精兵之手，圍城數月不得進，直到長春宮投降才得以合兵直趨河中。李懷光手下的都虞侯呂鳴岳曾密謀歸順馬燧，事泄後被李懷光殺死並誅及全家，這一事件加速了軍心的崩潰；最後朔方將牛名俊斬下李懷光首級，率萬餘名士卒開城出降，馬燧入城後只殺懷光親信閻晏等七人，其餘不復問罪。德宗本人則在建中四年到貞元元年之間面對財政困難與諸道觀望，屢次拒絕朝臣赦免李懷光的請求，把這場平叛拖成了持久圍城。
peopleEn: The decisive figures in this war are few in number. Li Huai-guang is the central character of the whole episode: after helping to break the siege at Fengtian, he considered his service of a thousand li to the emperor unrewarded because he was never allowed to see the throne, and he lodged memorial after memorial accusing Lu Qi, Zhao Zan and Bai Zhizhen; when the court exiled those three and then granted him the title of Grand Commandant together with an iron certificate of pardon, he threw the certificate on the ground before the envoy and said that a certificate given to a man who was about to rebel only drove him to rebel, and so he rose in arms. He did not join Zhu Ci, however; he retired to Hezhong to defend himself, and in the end, with his generals deserting and his supplies and reinforcements cut off, he hanged himself. Ma Su was the real commander of the campaign. Holding the office of jiedushi of Hedong, he first won over by persuasion the three prefectures that Li Huai-guang had left under the charge of his brother-in-law Yao Tingzhen at Jinzhou, his military commissioner Mao Chaoyi at Xizhou and Zheng Kang at Cizhou, thereby cutting off the northern support of Hezhong; he then broke Li's vanguard at Taocheng and shot his general Xu Bowen dead. Longchun Palace could not be taken, and rather than assault it he rode alone to its foot, called the name of its defender Xu Tingguang, stripped open his robe to show that he carried no weapon, and spoke of how these men had served the state since the rebellion of An Lushan for more than forty years and should not now scheme for the destruction of their own clan. Xu Tingguang and his men immediately made obeisance and surrendered, and once that gate of Hezhong had fallen the fortress lay wide open. Hun Jian, Luo Yuanguang and Tang Chaochen had been beaten repeatedly on the Tongzhou and Huazhou line by the six thousand elite troops of Xu Tingguang and had made no progress for months of siege; only after the surrender of Longchun Palace could they unite and drive straight at Hezhong. Li Huai-guang's military commissioner Lü Mingyue had once plotted to hand the city over to Ma Su; the plot was uncovered, Li killed him and wiped out his family, and the incident hastened the collapse of morale in the rebel ranks. Finally the Shuofang commander Niu Mingjun cut off Li Huai-guang's head and led more than ten thousand soldiers out of the city in submission, and Ma Su entered the city and executed only seven of Li's closest confidants, Yan Yan among them, sparing the rest. Dezong himself, between Jianzhong 4 and the first year of Zhengyuan, had to face exhausted finances and circuits that stood by and watched, and he rejected the repeated requests of his ministers to pardon Li Huai-guang, dragging the suppression of the revolt into a long siege.
kits: 卡面這柄羅馬短劍並沒有出現在唐軍的陣列裡，更沒有出現在河中的城頭。羅馬短劍是公元前第一個世紀成熟的雙刃刺擊短兵，劍身狹長約六十至七十公分，握柄下端有圓盤形柄頭，刃的前段略作收束，專門用來在貼身格鬥中刺入對手的盾縫、面門與腋下；它與大盾、重標槍組成羅馬軍團的標準配備，士兵先把標槍投出，再以短劍貼住盾邊往前送刺，卡面那句「刺劍不是用來揮砍的，短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏」，說的就是這條技術路線。而中唐的步兵體系走的是另一條路：唐軍近身主力是環首直刃刀，單刃無護手，長度與短劍相當，動作以劈砍為主，配合白刃長槍的槍陣與大盾構成縱深；遠射靠蹶張弩、擘張弩與角弓，壓制城頭的力道來自弩機與石砲而不是短兵。攻城一方，圍城期內官軍修築營壘、挖掘壕溝、列木柵，備雲梯、撞車、櫓與發石用的砲，把長春宮與河中包成兩個孤立的圈；本役的勝負卻不在器械，而在糧道與人心。防護上，唐軍有明光鎧、鎲甲、鱗甲與綿甲，頭戴皮兜鍪，騎兵是河東、朔方藩鎮最擅長的力量，蕃騎與漢騎混編；後勤靠牛馬挽車、黃河漕運與屯田，而河中藩鎮真正的財政支柱是解州一帶的河東鹽池，鹽要運往關中，必經蒲坂渡口過河，這條線一斷，河中與朝廷在物資上先輸了半步。
kitsEn: The Roman gladius on the card never appeared in the Tang ranks, and certainly not on the walls of Hezhong. The gladius was a double-edged thrusting short sword that matured in the first century BC: a narrow blade some sixty to seventy centimetres long, a disc-shaped pommel closing the grip, and a forward section slightly drawn to a point, made for stabbing into the gap beneath a shield, into a face or under an arm. Together with the large oval scutum and the heavy pilum it formed the standard kit of the Roman line, the legionary first throwing his javelin and then closing behind his shield to deliver the thrust, which is precisely the technical line described on the card: the thrusting sword is not swung, and close combat is decided by the edge of the shield and the rhythm of the stab. The mid-Tang infantry followed a different path. Its close-combat mainstay was the ring-pommel straight-edged dao, single-edged and without a guard, of a length comparable to the gladius, worked mainly by cutting, and it was combined with the long white-bladed spear and the large shield to form a layered formation; its firepower came from the crossbow, both the drawn-and-thrust and the drawn-and-stood types, and from the composite bow, and the pressure it brought against a wall came from crossbow bolts and stone-throwing engines rather than from short weapons. On the attacking side the besieging army built camp works, dug trench lines and planted wooden palisades, and brought scaling ladders, battering rams, siege sheds and stone-throwing engines to bear on the two isolated rings drawn around Longchun Palace and Hezhong; the outcome of this war lay not in equipment but in the grain route and in men's minds. For protection the Tang carried bright armour, iron lamellar, scale and padded mail, with leather-covered helmets, and their cavalry was the strength of the Hedong and Shuofang commands, barbarian and Chinese riders mixed. Logistics rested on ox and mule wagons, Yellow River transport and garrison farming, while the real financial pillar of the Hezhong command was the Hedong salt pans around Xiezhou, whose salt had to cross the Yellow River at the Pusan ferry to reach the central plain; once that line was cut, Hezhong had already lost the first half of the contest on materials.
tactics: 這場圍城戰可以分三段看。第一段是取外圍、斷羽翼：馬燧以河東節度使的權威與私誼，派人說降李懷光分守晉州、隰州、慈州的姻親要廷珍、牙將毛朝易和鄭抗，三州一失，李懷光北面的兵源與糧源立刻斷了，朝廷在兵法上叫先取其羽翼；與此同時，朝廷也派宦官尹元貞赴河中撫慰，並一度在朝議中有人主張赦免懷光以罷兵，均未採行。第二段是陶城野戰：馬燧合兵擊敗李懷光前鋒，射殺大將徐伯文，資治通鑑記斬首萬餘級，這是本役規模最大的一次正面交鋒，隨即與渾瑊、駱元光、唐朝臣會師，進逼長春宮。第三段是攻心與坐困：長春宮有徐庭光所率精兵六千，憑險而守，渾瑊、駱元光屢攻不下，馬燧遂捨攻城而取其心，單騎至城下直呼守將之名，陳說順逆，士卒伏泣，徐庭光遂開門羅拜而降；德宗聞之授他御史大夫，門戶一失，河中守軍分崩，諸將爭先出降，李懷光自縊，牛名俊斬首出城。整體打法可以歸納成三個字：不急攻、重斷糧、常說降。與卡面那柄短劍的路數相比更見分明，羅馬軍團的近戰靠的是三列縱深與盾邊刺突的節奏，而唐軍在河中城下靠的是弩砲壓制、城池坐困與一個人站在城下把守將說服。
tacticsEn: This siege can be read in three stages. The first was to strip away the outer posts and break the enemy's wings: Ma Su used the authority and the personal ties of his position as jiedushi of Hedong to win over Yao Tingzhen, Mao Chaoyi and Zheng Kang, who held Jinzhou, Xizhou and Cizhou for Li Huai-guang; the loss of the three prefectures cut away at once the northern supply of men and grain for Hezhong, which in military terms is to seize the enemy's wings first. At the same time the court sent the eunuch Yin Yuanzhen to soothe Li at Hezhong, and at one point ministers proposed pardoning him so as to end the war; neither course was adopted. The second stage was the open-field battle at Taocheng, where Ma Su united his forces, defeated Li's vanguard and shot the general Xu Bowen dead; the Zizhi Tongjian records that more than ten thousand heads were taken, and this was the largest single engagement of the campaign, after which he joined forces with Hun Jian, Luo Yuanguang and Tang Chaochen and pressed up to Longchun Palace. The third stage was a combination of psychological pressure and blockade. Longchun Palace was held by the six thousand elite of Xu Tingguang, who exploited the ground to hold out; repeated attacks by Hun Jian and Luo Yuanguang failed, and Ma Su therefore abandoned the assault and went after the garrison's heart, riding alone to the foot of the wall to call out the name of the defending general and set out the right and wrong of the cause, at which the soldiers wept; Xu Tingguang opened the gate and surrendered in a row of obeisance. Dezong heard of it and made him Censor-in-Chief, and once that gate had fallen the defenders of Hezhong came apart, the generals vying with one another to be the first to surrender, Li Huai-guang hanged himself, and Niu Mingjun came out with his head. The whole method can be summed up in three points: do not hurry the assault, cut the grain route, and keep talking of surrender. Set against the technique of the sword on the card, the contrast is plain, for the close fight of the Roman line was carried by depth of formation and the rhythm of the stab behind the shield, whereas the Tang army won the city of Hezhong by crossbow fire, by blockade, and by one man standing beneath the wall talking the garrison's commander into surrender.
data: 可核對的數字分四類。第一類是系年：建中四年（783）十月涇原兵變，朱泚據長安稱帝；德宗出奔奉天，次年正月還都；李懷光反出河中，圍城起於貞元元年（784）初，至三月長春宮降、河中城破。關於李懷光之死的年份，各家記載略有出入，資治通鑑、舊唐書、新唐書繫於貞元元年三月，換算即公元784年，戰爭一覽亦取784年；另有一些後世敘述與工具書繫於785年，屬貞元二年一系，諸說並存，本卡依前說。第二類是兵員與斬獲：資治通鑑記馬燧在陶城破敵斬首萬餘級，又記牛名俊斬李懷光首級後率萬餘名士卒開城出降；守長春宮的徐庭光率精兵六千；李懷光控制的藩鎮至少含河中、絳州、晉州、隰州、慈州五州，一節度使兼領數州節度使與行營副元帥的體例在中唐已固定，本役中馬燧、渾瑊各加授河中或晉、慈、隰等州節度使。第三類是距離與地理：河中府治蒲州在今山西永濟一帶，扼黃河蒲坂渡口，東北距長春宮（今陝西大荔東）約二百餘里，沿黃河東岸成一線；解州的河東鹽池產鹽，運往關中須經蒲坂陸運。第四類是存疑處：圍城各方兵員總數在傳世文獻中基本失傳，只留下斬首與降卒等局部數字；關中自建中初年起連年旱饑，軍需與轉運吃緊，度支用度不給，這是官軍不得不改取說降而非強攻的實在理由；至於交戰兵員的傷亡數字，史無可考，本卡不列。
dataEn: The verifiable figures fall into four kinds. First, chronology: in the tenth month of Jianzhong 4 (783) the Jingyuan mutiny broke out and Zhu Ci proclaimed himself emperor at Chang'an; Dezong fled to Fengtian and returned to the capital in the first month of the next year; Li Huai-guang broke out of Hezhong, the siege opened in the first months of Zhengyuan 1 (784), and in the third month Longchun Palace surrendered and the city of Hezhong fell. The year of Li Huai-guang's death is not uniform across the sources: the Zizhi Tongjian, the Jiu Tangshu and the Xin Tangshu place it in the third month of Zhengyuan 1, which converts to AD 784 and is also the year taken by the list of wars, while some later narratives and reference works place it in 785, a dating belonging to the second year of Zhengyuan; the two accounts stand side by side, and this card follows the former. Second, men and losses: the Zizhi Tongjian records that Ma Su took more than ten thousand heads at Taocheng, and that after Niu Mingjun cut off Li Huai-guang's head he led more than ten thousand soldiers out of the city in submission; Xu Tingguang, who held Longchun Palace, commanded six thousand picked men; and the command of Li Huai-guang covered at least the five prefectures of Hezhong, Jiangzhou, Jinzhou, Xizhou and Cizhou, the mid-Tang practice by which a single jiedushi was granted several prefectures together with the title of deputy commander of a field camp being already fixed, Ma Su and Hun Jian each receiving additional prefectural titles. Third, distances and geography: the seat of Hezhong at Puzhou lay in what is now Yongji in Shanxi, commanding the Pusan crossing of the Yellow River, some two hundred odd li to the north-east of Longchun Palace, which was east of modern Dali, the two forming a single line along the eastern bank of the river; the Hedong salt pans around Xiezhou produced salt that had to be carried overland through Pusan to reach the central plain. Fourth, the doubtful points: the total numbers on both sides are essentially lost, the records preserving only local figures of heads taken and men surrendered; the central plain suffered repeated drought and famine from the early Jianzhong years onward, transport and supply were strained and the treasury could not meet its needs, which is the real reason the court turned to persuasion rather than a direct assault; and figures for the casualties on either side are simply not recorded, so none are given here.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最外層是涇原兵變的衝擊：朱泚在長安稱帝，德宗出奔，朝廷倉促起用北疆藩鎮兵勤王，李懷光以朔方節度使之眾千里赴難，卻在咸陽屯兵不進，屢次上表揭發朝臣，數次不得與天子相見，怨氣積到朝廷貶盧杞、賜他太尉與鐵券那一刻爆開；他把鐵券擲在地上說是使反也，正說明君臣之間的最後一點互信已斷。第二層是藩鎮將領的自保邏輯：李懷光沒有投朱泚，也沒有打著勤王的旗號，他只是退回自己的地盤，河中節度使手握朔方精兵與河防要地，節度使的兵權、財權與人事權在中唐已高度獨立，一旦朝廷的信任崩了，最安全也最現實的選擇就是據河中以自保，等朝廷來談。第三層是朝廷的算盤：德宗收復長安之後，必須解決河東與河中的問題，蒲坂是關中漕運與河東鹽運的咽喉，不拿下河中，關中就永遠頂著北方藩鎮的壓力，而唐廷財力困窘，度支用度不給，強攻不現實，於是才有馬燧的單騎說降與三州之議。換言之，這是一場朝廷與藩鎮在財政與信任都見底的時候，憑意氣和辦法硬碰硬解決的叛亂。
causeEn: There were three layers to the outbreak. The outermost was the shock of the Jingyuan mutiny: with Zhu Ci proclaimed at Chang'an and Dezong in flight, the court hastily employed the frontier commands to raise troops for the emperor's relief, and Li Huai-guang led the Shuofang army a thousand li to the scene, only to sit at Xianyang without advancing, to file memorial after memorial against the ministers, and to be refused audience with the emperor several times; the grievance came to a head at the moment when the court exiled Lu Qi and granted him the title of Grand Commandant with an iron certificate of pardon, and his words as he threw the certificate down, that this was a way of driving him to rebel, mark the last of the trust between ruler and minister breaking. The second layer was the self-preserving logic of a frontier command: Li Huai-guang neither joined Zhu Ci nor claimed to be coming to the emperor's aid; he simply returned to his own ground, for a jiedushi of Hezhong held the picked troops of Shuofang and a position commanding the river, and the military, fiscal and personnel powers of such a jiedushi had become highly independent in the middle Tang; once the court's trust had failed, the safest and most immediate course was to hold Hezhong and wait for terms. The third layer was the court's own calculation: after regaining Chang'an, Dezong had to settle the question of Hedong and Hezhong, for Pusan was the throat of the central plain's transport and of the salt road from Hedong; without Hezhong the central plain would forever bear the pressure of the northern commands, and with exhausted finances and a treasury unable to meet its needs a frontal assault was unrealistic, hence the single rider at the foot of the wall and the proposal to take the three prefectures. In short this was a revolt settled by force of character and of method at a moment when the court's finances and trust had both run out.
impact: 平定河中之亂的直接後果，是唐廷在中原重新拿回了主動權。建中四年以來接連兩場叛亂，涇原兵變與李懷光之亂，都被壓下去；李懷光死後，其殘部與其子李琟的勢力延續到貞元二年才告清平，殘餘的處置方式各家記載不一。制度上最要緊的變化有三。其一，河中節度使的建制並未因李懷光之死而廢，河中仍是唐廷在河東的關鍵藩鎮，蒲坂的鹽運與漕運重新掌握在朝廷可以施壓的節度使手裡，這條線關係到建中元年楊炎推行兩稅法之後唐廷日益依賴的鹽利收入。其二，德宗借平叛之威整頓軍令，馬燧以河東節度使兼討平首功入朝，渾瑊、駱元光等各加官晉爵，神策軍在李晟手上收復長安、掃平朱泚殘部，禁軍的重建與藩鎮的削弱同時推進，卻也生出新的跋扈問題。其三，在人心與名聲的層面，賜鐵券而反的李懷光成了恩重而不受節制的樣板，馬燧單騎入城下說降守將則被後世反覆講述，成為唐代名將功業的樣板，兩面都寫進了此後對忠將與叛將的評價。往後看，藩鎮割據的大格局並未因這一役改變，河東、河中依然是唐廷的隱患，德宗朝在軍令與將才這一層短暫恢復的元氣，也僅止於此。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the suppression of the Hezhong revolt was that the Tang court recovered the initiative in the central plain. Two rebellions in succession from Jianzhong 4 onwards, the Jingyuan mutiny and the revolt of Li Huai-guang, were both put down; after Li's death his remaining followers and the forces of his son Li Pu lingered until the second year of Zhengyuan before the matter was finally closed, and the accounts differ on how the remnants were disposed of. Three institutional changes matter most. First, the office of jiedushi of Hezhong was not abolished with Li Huai-guang's death; Hezhong remained the key command of the court in Hedong, and the salt and grain routes of Pusan passed back into hands in which the court could apply pressure, a line tied to the salt revenues on which the Tang increasingly depended after Yang Yan had introduced the two-tax system in the first year of Jianzhong. Second, Dezong used the prestige of the victory to tighten military discipline: Ma Su entered the capital as jiedushi of Hedong with the credit of having ended the revolt, Hun Jian, Luo Yuanguang and others were raised in rank, and the Divine Strategy Army under Li Sheng retook Chang'an and swept up Zhu Ci's remnants, so that the rebuilding of the imperial guard and the reduction of the frontier commands advanced together, though at the cost of fresh instances of overbearing generals. Third, at the level of reputation and sentiment, Li Huai-guang, who had rebelled despite an iron certificate of pardon, became the type of the man who accepts great favour but refuses restraint, while Ma Su's single ride to the foot of the wall to talk the garrison into surrender was retold for generations as a model of what a great Tang general could do; both images were written into the later judgement of loyal generals and rebels. Looking forward, the great structure of regional military command was not altered by this war; Hedong and Hezhong remained the chronic hidden trouble of the court, and the vigour that the reign of Dezong recovered lay only and briefly in the sphere of command and of generalship.
result: 貞元元年（784）三月，結局以一種奇特的安靜收場。李懷光在長春宮投降、諸將接連出降之後，判斷大勢已去，在河中自縊而死；朔方將牛名俊斬下他的首級，率萬餘名士卒開城出降，馬燧入城，殺掉懷光的親信閻晏等七人，其餘一概不問罪，兵不血刃地完成了對河中城的接管。戰役層面，馬燧在陶城打掉了李懷光唯一一支能野戰的部隊，斬首萬餘級；徐庭光以六千精兵據守的長春宮，則在圍城數月、屢攻不下之後，因守將被說服而開門，這是唐代圍城戰中最被後世記住的一次攻心取城。留下的教訓同樣清楚：藩鎮軍隊對朝廷的效忠，往往不及對主帥與待遇的效忠，李懷光自毀於呂鳴岳謀降被誅與全城軍心崩潰；反過來，朝廷能以不大的代價拿下河中，靠的也不是強攻，而是先取晉、隰、慈三州切斷其北面，陶城一戰摧其前鋒，再以單騎說降破其門戶。河中之亂平定，河中重新歸入唐室版圖，李懷光的頭顱送到行在；戰後降卒被收編分隸各軍，蒲坂的鹽運與漕運重新在朝廷任命的節度使手裡運轉，河中藩鎮的建制亦完整保留了下來，而藩鎮的問題卻一場也沒有少。
resultEn: In the third month of Zhengyuan 1 (784) the affair ended with a strange quietness. After the surrender of Longchun Palace and the successive surrenders of his generals, Li Huai-guang judged the situation lost and hanged himself at Hezhong; the Shuofang commander Niu Mingjun cut off his head and led more than ten thousand soldiers out of the city in submission; Ma Su entered the city and killed the seven closest confidants of the rebel, Yan Yan among them, sparing everyone else, so that the transfer of the city of Hezhong was completed without the shedding of blood on its walls. In tactical terms, Ma Su destroyed at Taocheng the only field army Li Huai-guang could put into battle, taking more than ten thousand heads; and Longchun Palace, held by six thousand picked men of Xu Tingguang, opened after months of unsuccessful siege, not to a storm but because its commander was talked into surrender, the assault by words that later ages remembered as the classic Tang siege by psychological operation. The lesson is equally clear: the loyalty of a frontier command's troops to the court rarely exceeded their loyalty to their commander and their pay, and Li Huai-guang destroyed himself over the plot of Lü Mingyue and the collapse of morale in the city; conversely, the court took Hezhong at no great cost, and not by force, but by first taking Jinzhou, Xizhou and Cizhou to cut the north, then one battle at Taocheng to shatter the vanguard, and then a single rider's words to open the gate. The revolt of Hezhong was settled and Hezhong returned to the empire, and Li Huai-guang's head was carried to the imperial camp; afterwards the surrendered men were enrolled and distributed among the various armies, the salt road and the grain traffic of Pusan began to run again in the hands of a jiedushi appointed by the court, and the administrative structure of the Hezhong command was preserved entire; the frontier questions of the middle Tang, however, were not thereby answered.
